title: Mass Air Flow (MAF) and Intake Air Temperature (IAT) Sensor
introduction:
This procedure applies to the 5.2L engine in the Electronic Engine Controls — 32V Ti-VCT section. The combined mass air flow and intake air temperature sensor is the intake's small reporting desk: its name identifies the airflow and temperature information it supplies.

I use the drawing to find the blue sensor on the intake duct beside the ribbed hose. The magenta connector and retainers identify what comes off before the sensor can be removed. This is a removal-and-installation guide; it does not establish that the sensor is faulty or provide a cleaning, electrical-testing or diagnostic procedure.

items.name: Confirm the engine and identify the component
items.detail: Use this procedure only for the identified engine application. Match the sensor and connector to the intake-duct illustration before disconnecting anything. Have a suitable retainer tool and a torque tool capable of accurately applying the installation setting shown in the removal step; the tool size is not specified.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle so another person cannot start it during service; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. If remote start is fitted, disable it through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the vehicle. Otherwise the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, causing personal injury or death. On vehicles equipped with engine auto start-stop, ignition ON can permit an automatic start; keep it OFF when working near rotating engine parts, or serious personal injury may result.

items.name: Wear the required protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service; failure to do so may cause serious personal injury. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges; those edges can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Check cooling fans before underhood work
items.detail: With the ignition OFF, inspect all cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation. Do not work under the hood with a damaged fan; replace it with a new fan before proceeding because it can separate during operation and cause serious personal injury. Fans may run even with the ignition OFF. Disable them before working nearby to prevent unexpected operation and personal injury.

edits.text: Remove the MAF and IAT sensor
NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they may also contain details needed during installation.
edits.why: The retainer-tightening specification appears beside removal. I keep that detail in view for reassembly so it does not get lost in the rush to put the intake back together.

edits.text: Disconnect the combined mass air flow (MAF) and intake air temperature (IAT) sensor electrical connector before removing the sensor retainers.
edits.why: The drawing identifies the connector at the end of the sensor. Disconnecting it first separates the wiring from the part that will be lifted out; the illustration does not establish a particular connector-unlocking motion.

edits.text: Remove the retainers, then remove the combined mass air flow (MAF) and intake air temperature (IAT) sensor from the intake duct. During installation, tighten the retainers to 18 lb.in (2 Nm).
edits.why: The blue sensor flange and magenta fasteners show the mounting points beside the ribbed intake hose. The stated torque is the installation setting, not an instruction to apply torque while removing the fasteners.

edits.text: Refit the MAF and IAT sensor
Reverse the removal sequence: refit the sensor in the intake duct, install and tighten its retainers to the specification given in the removal step, then reconnect the electrical connector.
edits.why: This restores the mechanical mounting before the electrical connection. Confirm that the retainers are installed and the connector is reconnected. Completion here means reassembly; the procedure supplies no functional test or basis for declaring an airflow or temperature complaint repaired.
